4: Shivaji 74-80 Bhonsle, born 19 February 1630 to Shahji and Jijabai, takes his first fort at 16 (1646) from the forested Maval, guided by Dadaji Kondadev.
He attacks Bijapur (1657), kills Afzal Khan (1659), sacks Surat (1663). Jai Singh 99-43 besieges Purandhar in 1665, so Shivaji 74-80 gives up 23 of 35 forts.
Crowned Chhatrapati at Raigarh in 1674, free of the Mughals after the 1666 Agra escape. 240 forts, a navy of 200 ships by 1664; officials paid cash, no Jagirs.
Eight ministers, the Ashtapradhan, headed by the Peshwa as PM, run the State. Twelve Darakhdars form the Barbhai Mandal in 1774 under Nana Fadnavis. Villages have a Patil.
Sambhaji 80-89 is killed in 1689, Rajaram 89-00 dies in 1700. Regent Tarabai rules till 1707, when Shahu 19-49 is released and civil war starts, lasting to 1719.
Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath 13-20 wins bankers and Sardars for Shahu 19-49, who wins. Four Sardars (Gaikwad, Holkar, Scindia, Bhonsle) rise: Peshwa rules Svarajya, Sardars rule Samrajya from 1719.
Chauth is 25% of a protected state's revenue; the drain weakens it until a short war annexes it. Sardeshmukhi: extra 10%. Sardars abroad keep 66% (Mokasa), send 25% (Babti).
Balaji Vishwanath 13-20 allies with the Sayyid Brothers (1719) and wins Chauth rights; the Nizam stops paying in 1724. Then Delhi is plundered in 1737 by Baji Rao 20-40.
Three Peshwas in a row make the post hereditary. Nana Saheb (1740-61) makes Ramraja sign the Treaty of Sangola in February 1750: all real power to the Peshwa.
Raghunath Rao 73-74 expels Abdali's son Timur from Lahore in March 1758. Abdali (60,000) with allies faces Sadasiv Rao Bhau (50,000); supply cut, Bhonsle refuses, about 50,000 die.
Weak Peshwas follow; Mahadji Scindia 68-94 retakes Delhi in 1771. The EIC takes Delhi in 1803, annexes Svarajya 1817-19. The Marathas took tribute, never ruled.
5: Fight on or lose the land: so the middle path. Rebel becomes Mansabdar, pays tribute, gives an army; emperor gives dynastic governorship, Watan Jagir. Sikhs stay outside.
Besides the Marathas: the Jat Kingdom of Bharatpur, Farrukhabad (1714, Bangash Pathans) and Rohilkhand (Rohillas). All turned local force into rule; none built a big empire.
Heavy land revenue and lost autonomy under Jahangir 05-27 push Jat Zamindars into guerrilla resistance. Gokla (1669), then Churaman 95-21 founds Bharatpur in 1695; Badan Singh (1722-55) consolidates.
Surajmal 56-63 builds a centralised State, Delhi to Agra, with Lohagarh. At Panipat 1761 Bhau rejects his guerrilla plan. After he dies in 1763 the State collapses.
Afghans came as warlords for hire. Farid Khan (born about 1486) learns Mughal administration after 1526, and by 1540 as Sher Shah 40-45 beats Humayun 30-40 at Kanauj.
In five years Sher Shah 40-45 builds Suba-Sarkar-Pargana, the Grand Trunk Road, Dak Chowki, the silver Rupiya and fair revenue with Patta and Qubuliat. After 1545 the Afghans fragment.
Md Khan Bangash backs Farrukhsiyar 13-19 with 12,000 troops and founds Farrukhabad in 1714. Son Qaim Khan falls to Safdar Jung 39-54's scheme in 1749; Awadh annexes Farrukhabad.
Ahmad Khan Bangash 50-71 retakes Farrukhabad (1750), is driven out, returns by ceding half to Holkar and Scindia. Beside Abdali in 1761 he regains all; EIC annexes it 1802.
Katehr Zamindars hire Afghan Rohillas; Ali Md Khan leads them from 1721. In 1739 Nadir Shah paralyses Delhi, so he stops taxes; in 1740 he is made Subadar.
Najib-ud-Daula 57-70 backs Abdali in 1761; Delhi is under Rohilla influence till Mahadji Scindia 68-94 retakes it in 1771. In 1774 Awadh and the EIC annex most of Rohilkhand.
In March 1758 Raghunath Rao 73-74 drives Abdali's son Timur Shah out of Lahore. To avenge Timur Shah is Abdali's immediate reason for Third Panipat.
Each rose differently, yet each needed an outside prop: Abdali for the Afghan kingdoms, Maratha backing for Surajmal 56-63. The props went (Abdali 1761, Surajmal's death 1763) and they fell.
6: Guru Nanak Dev (1469-1539) teaches one formless God, no rituals or priests, no caste, honest living. He settles at Kartarpur and starts the Langar, a free kitchen for equality.
A State needs territory; once Sikhs demand one at Anandpur, conflict begins. In 1606 Jahangir 05-27 executes the 5th Guru, Arjan Dev, and the movement turns martial.
In 1675 Aurangzeb 58-07 has the 9th Guru, Teg Bahadur, executed. In 1699 Gobind Singh 76-08 founds the Khalsa at Anandpur, an army like NSG or STF.
In December 1704 two elder sons die at Chamkaur; two younger are buried alive by Wazir Khan's order. Bahadur Shah 07-12 promises Anandpur in 1707, never kept.
Wazir Khan's assassins strike the Guru at Nanded in 1708 and he dies. Days before, he made the Guru Granth Sahib final Guru, to stop Jat versus Khatri tension.
Banda Bahadur 08-15 carries on: on 10 May 1710 he kills Wazir Khan and builds a State with coins, officials and seal. Farrukhsiyar 13-19 sends Abdus Samad Khan.
Khatri traders, hurt by war, are won over by Ijaradari and Mansabs; Jat zamindars switch, as Churaman 95-21 goes over. Banda Bahadur 08-15, no Guru, is executed in 1716.
Mughals are too weak to retake Punjab, so power spreads to Misl chiefs, kinship clans that unite against Afghans. By 1770 there are 12 major Misls: a weak centre.
Zaman Shah's invasions are the opportunity for Ranjit Singh 01-39: he takes Lahore from the Bhangi Misl, is crowned Maharaja in 1801, and makes other chiefs tribute-paying vassals.
Metcalfe's Treaty of Amritsar (1809) makes Ranjit Singh 01-39 sovereign with the Sutlej as border, so he expands: Multan 1818, Kashmir 1819, Peshawar 1834. Tripartite Treaty 1838 follows.
Ranjit Singh 01-39 balances Misl chiefs, the Khalsa army, Khatri traders and non-Sikh nobles. Only 40% is Jagirdari; Kardars collect the rest. Azizuddin and Dina Nath are ministers.
7: Already Autonomous States: the Rajputs came into the system but kept their homes, Travancore was never Mughal, Mysore grew from Vijayanagar. None followed the Mughal middle path.
Rajputana had about 20 clans and no centre; fighting them all was costly, so Akbar 56-05 made powerful chiefs Mansabdars with Vatan Jagirs, for tribute and troops.
Mewar under Raj Singh expands, so Aurangzeb 58-07 grows uneasy and in 1680 interferes in Marwar. Marwar and Mewar revolt, but other chiefs fear Mewar and refuse: it collapses.
After 1707 the Rajputs act on their own terms, like Sawai Jai Singh 99-43. Marathas raid from 1751; after 1803-05 the EIC replaces them with Subordinate Alliances.
Sawai Jai Singh 99-43 wears four hats: Mansabdar, state-builder, astronomer, town planner. Hurda 1734 fails and Bhopal 1738 gives Malwa to the Marathas; he founds Jaipur in 1727.
Jai Singh's Jantar Mantars stand at five cities; Jaipur's is largest. Old tables had errors, so fresh observations gave the Zij-i-Muhammad Shahi (1733), dedicated to Muhammad Shah 19-48.
Marthanda Varma 29-58 builds Travancore on trade: subdues chiefs, holds the Malabar trade monopoly, funds army and irrigation. In 1741 he crushes the Dutch at Colachel.
Rama Varma 58-98 prefers art to arms; Haider Ali 61-82 annexes Malabar and Calicut in 1766. Travancore signs a Subsidiary Alliance in 1805; Velu Thampi's 1809 Kundara Proclamation fails.
After Talikota (1565), Mysore turns autonomous under the Wodeyars; Chikka Devaraja 72-04 Wodeyar makes it strong. By 1761 PM NanjRaj makes them figureheads; Haider Ali 61-82 overthrows him.
With French help Haider Ali 61-82 builds Risalas and spends about twenty years subduing Poligars and Deshmukhs. Military Fiscalism pays for it: more Khalisa land, less Jagirdari, direct collection.
Tipu 82-99 runs a state trading company and uses iron rockets. In 1785 he declares independence and sets up embassies abroad; the French alliance gives no military support.
Mysore wanted all South India, but constant war drained it faster than Military Fiscalism refilled it. Four Anglo-Mysore wars ended with Tipu 82-99's death at Seringapatam in 1799.
